before.title: Local Einstein-scalar evolution: smooth constrained data admit a local development, unique up to a data-fixing isometry
before.statement:
Let $(\varphi,V,K)$ be the scalar-field matter model of
[[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]] with smooth potential $V$, and let
$(\Sigma,h,K_2,\varphi_0,\pi_0)$ be smooth initial data: a smooth three-manifold
$\Sigma$ with Riemannian metric $h$, symmetric $2$-tensor $K_2$, and smooth
functions $\varphi_0,\pi_0$ on $\Sigma$ (the scalar value and its prescribed
normal derivative). Suppose the constraint equations of
[[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] hold on $\Sigma$, computed with
the scalar stress-energy tensor determined by $(h,K_2,\varphi_0,\pi_0)$ and the
chosen unit normal. Then the data admit a local development in the sense of
[[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]: a smooth Lorentzian metric $g$ and
scalar field $\varphi$ near $\Sigma$ satisfying
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa\,T_{ab},\qquad \Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$$
with $T$ the scalar stress tensor, $\Sigma$ spacelike of induced metric $h$ and
second fundamental form $K_2$, and $\varphi|_\Sigma=\varphi_0$,
$\partial_n\varphi|_\Sigma=\pi_0$; and any two such developments of the same
data agree near $\Sigma$ up to a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving
isometry.

references.title: H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 5.4 (Matter Models): the conditions defining a matter model and the treatment of scalar-field matter coupled to the Einstein equations

H. Friedrich and A. D. Rendall, The Cauchy Problem for the Einstein Equations, Living Reviews in Relativity 3 (2000), article 1 (arXiv:gr-qc/0002074), Section 5.1 (Local Existence Theorems for the Einstein Equations): harmonic-map gauge, the reduced initial data constructed from (h,chi), the propagation of the gauge by the homogeneous wave system for the gauge residual Delta^alpha, and the local existence theorem

statement.after:
Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$, $\kappa>0$ and one scalar model $(\varphi,V,K_\phi)$ of [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]], with its fixed smooth potential and normalization. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, symmetric tensor $K_2$ and complete scalar data $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$. Suppose the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] hold for the scalar stress computed from these data, with $\pi_0$ the prescribed future-normal derivative. Then there is a smooth local Einstein-scalar development
$$G_{ab}+\Lambda g_{ab}=\kappa T_{ab},\qquad \Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,$$
with induced geometric data $(h,K_2)$, $\varphi|_\Sigma=\varphi_0$ and $n(\varphi)|_\Sigma=\pi_0$. The neighborhood may have position-dependent time width. The initial surface is interior to its intrinsic domain of dependence; restricting to the interior Cauchy neighborhood gives a globally hyperbolic development. Every two developments of this same fixed model and complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching $\varphi$. No potential positivity, mass sign, global existence or uniform noncompact slab is asserted ([[thm-gr-local-geometric-development]]).

citations.quote:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and
let $(\varphi,V,K)$ be the scalar-field matter model with scalar equation
$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$ and candidate stress-energy tensor
$T_{ab}=K[\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi-g_{ab}(\tfrac12\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi+V(\varphi))]$
([[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]). Fix a chart and the background
$\bar g,\bar\nabla$ of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. Then
the system consisting of the reduced Einstein equation with this $T$ and the
scalar equation, together with the definition of the auxiliary variables
$$u:=\bigl(g_{ab},\bar\nabla_0g_{ab},\bar\nabla_ig_{ab},\ \varphi,\ \varphi_0:=\bar\nabla_0\varphi,\ \varphi_i:=\bar\nabla_i\varphi\bigr)$$
is, on every region where the metric is Lorentzian and the chart is initially
orthogonal, a first-order quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system whose time
matrix is block diagonal with positive definite blocks: the metric block
$\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ of
[[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]] clause (b) and, for the scalar
variables, a positive definite block built from $1$ and $-g^{00}$; the coupling
between the metric and scalar blocks is only through zeroth-order terms in the
first derivatives of $g$. Moreover the stress-energy tensor is on-shell
divergence-free: $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ whenever $\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0$
([[prop-gr-scalar-field-stress-energy-conservation]]).

Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold, let $h$ be a smooth Riemannian metric
and $K$ a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor on $\Sigma$
([[def-gr-spacelike-initial-data-and-constraints]]). Let a **matter sector** be
specified as follows: a finite list of tensor fields $\psi$ on a spacetime
carrying $\Sigma$, a smooth stress-energy construction $T(g,\psi)$ and a system
of equations $E(g,\psi)=0$ such that, in every chart, the combined system for
$(\psi,g)$ with the metric variables of
[[lem-gr-reduced-einstein-principal-part]] clause (b) attached is a first-order
quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic system coupled only through zeroth-order terms
in the first derivatives of the metric, and such that $\nabla^aT_{ab}=0$ is a
consequence of $E(g,\psi)=0$ on-shell. Suppose smooth initial data $\psi_0$ on
$\Sigma$ are given so that the constraint equations
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa\,T(n,n),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK(Y)-\nabla^h_Y\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa\,T(n,Y)$$
hold on $\Sigma$ for the normal vector $n$ and the stress tensor determined by
$(h,K,\psi_0)$ ([[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]]). Then:

**(a)** every $p\in\Sigma$ has an open neighborhood $O_p$ in $\Sigma$ such that
there are an open neighborhood $W_p$ of $O_p$ in a smooth four-manifold, a smooth
Lorentzian metric $g$ and matter fields $\psi$ on $W_p$ solving the field
equations $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T(g,\psi)$ and the matter equations, with
$O_p$ a spacelike embedded hypersurface of induced metric $h$ and second
fundamental form $K$;

**(b)** the local solutions of (a) glue: over a neighborhood $W$ of $\Sigma$
there are $g,\psi$ solving the equations, with $\Sigma$ spacelike of data
$(h,K)$, and $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its domain of dependence in $W$,
so that $D(\Sigma)\cap W$ is an open globally hyperbolic neighborhood of
$\Sigma$ with $\Sigma$ as a Cauchy hypersurface and $(g,\psi)$ restricts to a
globally hyperbolic development of the data;

**(c)** any two developments as in (a)--(b) of the same data are related near
$\Sigma$ by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry
([[thm-gr-local-geometric-uniqueness]]).

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric
$h$, future unit normal field $n$ and second fundamental form
$K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]],
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Let
$s$ be a smooth function defined near $\Sigma$ with $s=0$ exactly on $\Sigma$
and $ds(n)=1$ (a normal time coordinate), and let $h_0$ be a smooth metric on a
product neighborhood of $\Sigma$ with $h_0|_{\Sigma}=h$ and
$\partial_sh_0=0$. Put $\bar g:=-ds^2+h_0$ as background metric. Define a smooth
metric germ $g_0$ on $\Sigma$ by the initial jet
$$g_{ij}=h_{ij},\qquad g_{00}=-1,\qquad g_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{ij}=2K_{ij},\qquad \partial_sg_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{00}=-2\operatorname{tr}_hK .$$
Then:

**(a)** $g_0$ is the germ of a smooth Lorentzian metric for which $\Sigma$ is
spacelike with induced metric $h$, future unit normal $n=\partial_s$ and second
fundamental form $K$;

**(b)** the harmonic-gauge vector of $(g_0,\bar g)$ vanishes on $\Sigma$:
$H^a|_\Sigma=0$.

derivations.claim: (Verification of the matter hypotheses.) By [L1] the scalar sector satisfies both hypotheses of [L2]: the combined system is first-order quasilinear symmetric hyperbolic with zeroth-order coupling, and the stress tensor is on-shell conserved.

(Application of the development theorem.) Applying [L2] with the data $(\Sigma,h,K_2)$ and the matter data $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$ (whose normal derivative is the prescribed $\pi_0$ and whose jet is the one of [L3]) yields a smooth metric and scalar field near $\Sigma$ satisfying the field equation with the scalar stress tensor and the scalar equation, with the stated induced data and normal derivative, together with the causal and uniqueness conclusions.

boundaries.reason: No empty set, empty family or empty index range is formed: the quantified objects (points, fields, mode families, data sets) are nonempty by the hypotheses, and the proofs never split off an empty case.
The value zero is not a distinguished boundary of this claim: no step divides by a quantity that can vanish and no separate zero case is required.
No cardinality-one case is separated: the arguments treat general finite or countable families and the one-element case is included without special treatment.

The hypotheses exclude degenerate configurations: the metric is Lorentzian/nondegenerate, the time matrix or coefficient is positive definite, velocity fields are unit and nonzero where required, and no degenerate limit is claimed.
The assertions are local in open domains around the initial surface or open time intervals, and no endpoint behaviour (completeness, boundary extension or endpoint regularity) is claimed.
No nonconstructive selection from a family is made: the argument uses the objects named in the Given clause and the supplied maps, with at most finite choices.
The item states one-directional implications or constructions, not an equivalence, so no forward direction of an if-and-only-if is asserted.
The item states one-directional implications or constructions, not an equivalence, so no reverse direction of an if-and-only-if is asserted.

after.quote:
Fix one scalar model with smooth potential $V$ and fixed stress normalization $K_\phi$ as in [[def-gr-scalar-field-matter-model]]. On a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold its equations and stress are
$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad T_{ab}=K_\phi\left[\partial_a\varphi\partial_b\varphi-g_{ab}\left(\tfrac12g^{cd}\partial_c\varphi\partial_d\varphi+V(\varphi)\right)\right].$$
Fix a chart and a smooth background $\bar g$ for the reduced Einstein equation of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]]. On the open state set where $g^{00}<0$ and $(g^{ij})$ is positive definite, the reduced Einstein equation coupled to this scalar equation has a smooth first-order symmetric hyperbolic reduction with variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},\varphi,P=\partial_0\varphi,Q_i=\partial_i\varphi).$$
The time matrix is block diagonal with metric block $\operatorname{diag}(I,-g^{00}I,g^{ij}I)$ and scalar block $\operatorname{diag}(1,-g^{00},g^{ij})$. Matter and metric cross-coupling is zeroth order in derivatives of $z$. The partial-derivative metric variables and the background-covariant ones are related by an invertible smooth zeroth-order change of variables; either gives the reduction.

For complete initial scalar data $(\varphi_0,\pi_0)$ in an initially orthogonal chart with $\partial_0=n$, prescribe $(\varphi,P,Q_i)=(\varphi_0,\pi_0,\partial_i\varphi_0)$. The auxiliary constraints propagate, the reconstructed scalar solves its full equation on the reduced metric, and its stress is conserved there before imposing the unreduced Einstein equation. Conversely every smooth physical scalar solution extracts to the same system. No potential positivity or mass sign is required; local arguments do not require a global orientation.

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Fix $\kappa>0$, $\Lambda\in\mathbb R$ and one covariant matter model: specified smooth fields $\Psi$, equations $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ and stress expression $\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Pullback by local diffeomorphisms commutes with these equations and stress expression. Let $\Sigma$ be a smooth three-manifold without boundary, with smooth Riemannian metric $h$, smooth symmetric tensor $K$ and complete smooth matter Cauchy data $d$. The sign convention is $K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ for the future unit normal. Initial matter tensors involving normal directions are specified on the abstract bundle $\mathcal V=\mathbb RN\oplus T\Sigma$, with metric $g_0(aN+X,bN+Y)=-ab+h(X,Y)$, rather than on a pre-existing spacetime.

Require the following explicit reduction hypotheses on each sufficiently small relatively compact initial coordinate ball with labels $x^i$, flat comparison metric $\bar g=-(dx^0)^2+\sum_i(dx^i)^2$, and finite variables
$$z=(g_{ab},p_{ab}=\partial_0g_{ab},q_{abi}=\partial_ig_{ab},w).$$

1. There are fixed smooth extraction and reconstruction rules and fixed smooth coefficient functions $A^\mu(x,z),B(x,z)$ on an open state set $O$ giving a system
$$A^0(x,z)\partial_0z+\sum_i A^i(x,z)\partial_iz+B(x,z)=0,$$
with symmetric $A^\mu$ and positive definite $A^0$. Its metric equations are exactly the first-order reduction of the reduced Einstein equations of [[def-gr-harmonic-gauge-and-reduced-equations]], with stress $T=\mathcal T(g,\Psi)$. Every smooth physical solution of this fixed model in harmonic coordinates extracts to this same system. Any internal matter gauge is already fixed with its specified equations and complete data; otherwise state the corresponding internal gauge equivalence in the conclusion.
2. Complete data determine a smooth initial value $w=\mathcal I(h,K,d)$, including all auxiliary variables and their compatibility constraints. The initial metric jet displayed in step 1.1 and this value lie in $O$. The reduction propagates its auxiliary compatibility constraints, so the reconstructed fields solve $\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0$ on the reduced solution, before imposing $H=0$ or the unreduced Einstein equations. The initial reconstruction induces exactly $d$ and the specified initial stress.
3. Whenever the reconstructed metric and fields satisfy those matter equations, their stress obeys $\nabla^a\mathcal T(g,\Psi)_{ab}=0$, independently of the unreduced Einstein equations. In particular this applies to the reduced solution furnished by clause 2. This is stronger than conservation asserted only after the full coupled equations have been proved.

These are concrete PDE, initialization and reconstruction hypotheses; they do not assume existence or geometric uniqueness. Require the constraints of [[thm-gr-constraint-equations-in-normal-frame]] for the stress determined by $(h,K,d)$:
$$S_h+(\operatorname{tr}_hK)^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T_0(N,N),\qquad \operatorname{div}_hK-d\operatorname{tr}_hK=\kappa T_0(N,\cdot).$$

Then the data have a smooth time-oriented local development $(g,\Psi)$ on an open variable-width neighborhood of $\{0\}\times\Sigma$ in the literal manifold $\mathbb R\times\Sigma$, with induced data $(h,K,d)$, solving
$$G(g)+\Lambda g=\kappa\mathcal T(g,\Psi),\qquad\mathcal E(g,\Psi)=0.$$
After restriction to a smaller collar, $\Sigma$ lies in the interior of its intrinsic domain of dependence. The interior of that domain is a globally hyperbolic neighborhood with $\Sigma$ Cauchy. Any two developments of this same model and these complete data are related near the entire initial surface by a data-fixing time-orientation-preserving isometry matching all matter fields. There is no uniform noncompact time width or global-in-time conclusion.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let
$\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a spacelike embedded hypersurface with induced metric
$h$, future unit normal field $n$ and second fundamental form
$K(V,W)=g(\nabla_Vn,W)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]],
[[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Let
$s$ be a smooth function defined near $\Sigma$ with $s=0$ exactly on $\Sigma$
and $ds(n)=1$ (a normal time coordinate), and let $h_0$ be a smooth metric on a
product neighborhood of $\Sigma$ with $h_0|_{\Sigma}=h$ and
$\partial_sh_0=0$. Put $\bar g:=-ds^2+h_0$ as background metric. Define a smooth
metric germ $g_0$ on $\Sigma$ by the initial jet
$$g_{ij}=h_{ij},\qquad g_{00}=-1,\qquad g_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{ij}=2K_{ij},\qquad \partial_sg_{0i}=0,\qquad \partial_sg_{00}=-2\operatorname{tr}_hK .$$
Then:

**(a)** $g_0$ is the germ of a smooth Lorentzian metric for which $\Sigma$ is
spacelike with induced metric $h$, future unit normal $n=\partial_s$ and second
fundamental form $K$;

**(b)** the harmonic-gauge vector of $(g_0,\bar g)$ vanishes on $\Sigma$:
$H^a|_\Sigma=0$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, and let $\Sigma\subseteq M$ be a smooth spacelike embedded hypersurface with future unit normal $n$, induced Riemannian metric $h$ and second fundamental form $K(X,Y)=g(\nabla_Xn,Y)$ ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]], [[lem-gr-spacelike-hypersurface-normal-and-second-fundamental-form]]). Write $D$ for the Levi-Civita connection of $h$, $R^h$ for its curvature operator in the same operator convention as the ambient curvature, and $S_h$ for its scalar curvature. Explicitly distinguish the lowered tensor from the operator pairing by setting
$$\mathcal R^g(A,B,C,D):=g(R^g(C,D)B,A),\qquad \mathcal R^h(A,B,C,D):=h(R^h(C,D)B,A).$$
Thus $\mathcal R^g_{abcd}=R_{abcd}$ in [[def-gr-curvature-tensor-and-derived-tensors]]; in particular $g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=\mathcal R^g(W,Z,X,Y)$. Let $G$ be the Einstein tensor defined there. At every $p\in\Sigma$ and for all $X,Y,Z,W\in T_p\Sigma$:

**(a) Gauss equation.**
$$\mathcal R^g(X,Y,Z,W)=\mathcal R^h(X,Y,Z,W)+K(X,Z)K(Y,W)-K(X,W)K(Y,Z).$$
Equivalently, in operator order,
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,W)=h(R^h(X,Y)Z,W)+K(Y,Z)K(X,W)-K(X,Z)K(Y,W).$$

**(b) Codazzi equation.**
$$g(R^g(X,Y)Z,n)=(D_YK)(X,Z)-(D_XK)(Y,Z).$$

**(c) Normal projections.** Define $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)=h^{ij}(D_{e_i}K)(e_j,Y)$, $\tau=\operatorname{tr}_hK=h^{ij}K_{ij}$ and $|K|_h^2=h^{ik}h^{jl}K_{ij}K_{kl}$. Then
$$G(n,n)=\tfrac12(S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2),\qquad G(n,Y)=(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau.$$

**(d) Constraint equations.** If the tensor equation $G+\Lambda g=\kappa T$ holds at $p$, for a smooth symmetric covariant $2$-tensor $T$ and real constants $\kappa,\Lambda$, then
$$S_h+\tau^2-|K|_h^2=2\Lambda+2\kappa T(n,n),\qquad (\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=\kappa T(n,Y).$$
With $\rho=T(n,n)$ and $j(Y)=-T(n,Y)$, the second equation is $(\operatorname{div}_hK)(Y)-D_Y\tau=-\kappa j(Y)$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be an oriented time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]],
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]), let $c>0$ be a fixed
real constant, and let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected connection of $g$
([[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]],
[[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]).

**(a) Data.** A **scalar-field matter model** on $M$ is a triple
$(\varphi,V,K)$ consisting of

- a smooth function $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$
  ([[def-c-r-and-smooth-maps-between-smooth-manifolds]], with target the
  standard one-dimensional smooth manifold $\mathbb R$);
- a smooth function $V:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$, the **potential**; and
- a real constant $K>0$, the **coupling**.

The physical reading of $K$ and of the units of $\varphi$ and $V$ is fixed by
the framework's matter postulate, not by this definition.

**(b) Scalar-action density and action differences.** For every smooth
function $\varphi'$ and every smooth Lorentzian metric $g'$ of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$ on $M$ define the **scalar-action density**

$$\ell(\varphi',g'):=-\frac{K}{c}\Bigl[\tfrac12\,g'^{ab}\,\partial_a\varphi'\, \partial_b\varphi'+V(\varphi')\Bigr]\mathrm{vol}_{g'}\in\Omega^4(M),$$

where $g'^{ab}$ are the inverse-metric components
([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]]) and
$\mathrm{vol}_{g'}$ the metric volume form
([[def-gr-metric-volume-form-and-current-flux]]). For two pairs $(\varphi,g)$
and $(\varphi',g')$ with $\varphi'-\varphi$ and all components of $g'-g$
supported in a compact set, the difference $\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)$
is a compactly supported smooth $4$-form and the **action difference**

$$\Delta S:=\int_M\bigl[\ell(\varphi',g')-\ell(\varphi,g)\bigr]$$

$$\Box_g\varphi-V'(\varphi)=0,\qquad \Box_g\varphi:=\nabla^a\partial_a\varphi,$$

covariant $2$-tensor field

$$T_{ab}:=K\Bigl[\partial_a\varphi\,\partial_b\varphi -g_{ab}\Bigl(\tfrac12\,\partial^c\varphi\,\partial_c\varphi+V(\varphi)\Bigr)\Bigr],$$

\partial_d\varphi$ ([[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]],

the Hilbert stress-energy tensor of the model, and that the scalar equation implies its conservation, are proved in
